doc.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26

title: Johnny Dodds and the others get cold feet
summary: Manetta had train tickets for Louis, Johnny Dodds and Joe Lindsey, but they backed out after the porters warned them.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So, uh, one day, I got out there then. Now, how it was, Frank Doosan had been out here, and they sent him back by not reading. And he said, here, he done sent the tickets to me on Lewis Armstrong, Johnny Dots, and Joe Lindsey. He's expecting. Of course, today, some fellas don't know that until today. I'm sure that happened now. I was going to get out. So, I had a ticket. I goes to Johnny Dots' house. Johnny Dots and his wife will accept me in. How to find him on a call. He had told his wife about it, but he had saw the porters at that porters inn on Rampart Street where the porters come in and bum, you know. Johnny Dots, they went to the porters and told the porters, well, he's going to leave, we're going to California. He said, who's going to California? He said, me, and all of them, and all of them. He said, what do you tell you, Johnny? He said, you better stay here because you're going to go out there and they're going to send you right back like they've done Frank Doosan. So, what Johnny does, he goes to work and see Lewis. At Patina Sartoga Lewis was living right there. He said, what do you tell me?

next to the ballroom. He goes with him and let's have a conversation over there. I don't know. I goes to his house. He didn't tell me. I noticed coming in a car, Louisiana Avenue car coming down. Now we come from Uptown to come see Dipper, get off at Petita and Rampart. I noticed he was kind of funny. He wouldn't say nothing. I said, well, he said, no, he wouldn't say nothing. So I said, well, I guess Dipper Rampart gets off. He goes down there, there's a little up in the place there, that ballroom there, a fella sitting on a bill box playing piano, a fella with a drum and lay at us, call it there. You know how he'd go for that. I can't go right. Yes, Mr. Hoss. Yes, Mr. Hoss. I said, oh, no, come outside. We talk about the wine. No wine.
